name: Marta Bralic Kerns
profile: Former Flatiron Health executive (a business-development leader on its executive team) who founded Pomelo Care in 2021 to deliver value-based, virtual maternity and newborn care alongside existing providers. Backed from seed by a16z and First Round Capital (a16z also led the Series A); Hurun lists the company at about $2B.
interesting_fact: She approached a16z partner Vineeta Agarwala — a former Flatiron colleague — in early 2021 with the idea; a16z co-led the seed with First Round and later led the Series A.
deep_cut_fact: She named the company after the pomelo fruit because its thick protective peel represents a protective layer around existing healthcare providers; early customer research was done in rural Georgia, more than an hour from an OB.
notes: Pomelo's website rate-limited (HTTP 429) and web-search budget was exhausted, so no published press email was found; check pomelocare.com press page manually. Valuation per Hurun Unicorn list (input).

name: Ricardo Mendes
profile: Co-founder and CEO of TEKEVER, founded in 2001 by IST computer scientists and AI researchers and bootstrapped from day one. It became Europe's leading maker of unmanned aerial systems (AR3, AR5, ARX) for maritime surveillance and defence, was declared a unicorn in 2025 and is opening factories in France and the UK.
interesting_fact: TEKEVER drones watch over the English Channel daily for the British government and fly from ships off Nigeria to counter piracy.
deep_cut_fact: Mendes frames drones simply as 'connected computers that move around', sorting them into logistics of information, of things and of people — and argues drone tech evolves at the speed of the internet, not aerospace.
notes: Common name — identify as TEKEVER CEO. Strong fit for an energy/infrastructure angle: TEKEVER drones survey oil pipelines in Africa and North America (per his 'Taking the Lead' piece).

name: Vineet Singh
profile: Listed by Darwinbox as one of its four co-founders alongside Chaitanya Peddi, Jayant Paleti and Rohit Chennamaneni. Darwinbox, founded in late 2015, sells a cloud HCM platform used by 1,400+ customers and 6M+ users in 130+ countries; it became a unicorn after a TCV-led $72M round (2022) and raised $140M from Partners Group and KKR in March 2025.
interesting_fact: Darwinbox was described as a rare Asian enterprise-software unicorn when TCV led its $72M round in January 2022.
notes: Lowest-profile of the Darwinbox founders: not named in the 2022 TechCrunch coverage (which lists three co-founders) but listed as co-founder on Darwinbox's 'Our Story' page. Common name — verify via Darwinbox. No personal details found before search budget ran out.
